messages:
maya: kicked off post-deploy smoke sweep (canary + stage). saw a gradual throttle on the text-gen route in us-west2, p95 doubled over ~3m.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: release/2026-03-23 -> canary. Postdeploy probes started (ci: 4825556666).
sam: quick triage: are we seeing 5xx, 429s, or timeouts?
maya: mostly 429s and a few 504s from the proxy. traces show requests queuing in inference-proxy; queue_length warnings in runtime metrics.
infra-ops: pulled metrics: proxy queue_length spiked to ~120 (baseline ~20) across proxy-usw2-*. worker threads at 100% CPU on a couple nodes.
beth: any config diffs in the new variant? batching / prefill changes?
maya: yes, v2026-03-23 bumped default batch_size 8 -> 16 to improve throughput. hypothesis: under low-concurrency short prompts this increases tail latency and queueing.
nora: proposal: hold global rollout and either pin us-west2 to previous variant or switch to a conservative batching profile for that region.
sam: agreed. Hold rollout. Action: pin us-west2 to v2026-03-21 and apply batching override conservative for the route while we validate.
infra-ops: executing pin+override:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/route/pin -d '{"region":"us-west2","model_variant":"v2026-03-21","overrides":{"batching_profile":"conservative"}}'
```
infra-ops: API returned 200 OK; routing pinned.
deploy-bot: Routing update complete for us-west2 -> v2026-03-21 (pinned). Synthetic scheduler queued 800 seeds with mixed prompt lengths.
maya: synthetic round 1: 429s dropped to baseline, p95 back near normal, CPU relieved on hotspot nodes.
beth: filing RT-6355: "batching-profile: increased batch_size causes tail-latency regression for short prompts". tagging runtime@, perf@.
sam: add to release notes: "us-west2 pinned to v2026-03-21 due to observed tail-latency increase in canary; investigating batching profile interaction." Do it now.
deploy-bot: Release notes updated.
maya: runbook next steps: 1) run A/B test with batch_size=8 vs 16 with telemetry; 2) reproduce locally with short prompt workload; 3) if instability recurs, plan canary rollback for affected pools.
sam: we'll monitor for 30m. If stable, we'll unpin and continue staged promote. If not, rollback canary tag and schedule follow-up postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
